changes: Added packages/solver, the deterministic matching seam from spec #2, with its own SolverCandidate/SolverVacancy input projections so ticket #4's CandidateProfile can adapt onto it later.
Implemented the weighted score (technical 30%, experience/evidence 25%, availability 15%, transport/accessibility 20%, salary/conditions 10%) with a per-dimension score breakdown and reasons.
Enforced the mandatory-skill, schedule, salary, capacity, and geographic (commute and accessibility) hard constraints; a failed constraint overrides the score and forces not_currently_apt.
Mapped scores to apt (75-100), apt_with_gaps (50-74), and not_currently_apt (0-49) via classifyAptitude.
Implemented the one-point promotion rule: it is only eligible with peer evidence that no better eligible candidate exists, and only applied with explicit human approval.
Made tie-breaking deterministic (score, failed-constraint count, vacancyId, candidateId) and independent of protected attributes and randomness.
Added a Google Maps Distance Matrix routing adapter that falls back to an offline local matrix and records why; all geographic reasons are surfaced.
Implemented the capacity-constrained assignment as a HiGHS MILP with a deterministic greedy fallback, wired into nominate().
Emitted MatchDecision as a JSON Schema 2020-12 contract validated with the shared Ajv instance from @puente/domain.
Added solver fixtures (metro-support, desirable-only, strong, mid, weak, credential-gap, infeasible-transport, schedule-conflict) and 76 Vitest tests.

validation.notes: 148/148 tests pass (76 new solver tests). Coverage 94.16% lines / 78.83% branches (gate-ci threshold is 80% lines / 70% branches). npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities. HiGHS runs in-process from a Wasm build; the real solver is exercised by an integration test and the greedy fallback by injected-failure tests.

blockedBy: #4 is not merged into main; the solver defines its own SolverCandidate input projection and provides the adaptation boundary instead of consuming CandidateProfile directly.
riskRemaining: Ticket #4 (CandidateProfile) is still unmerged, so the adapter from a candidate profile to SolverCandidate is not yet implemented; this is the explicit seam the profile ticket must satisfy. The default routing port uses the local matrix until GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY is configured, and the Google adapter is tested with an injected fetch rather than live calls. Protected attributes are structurally absent from the solver input; the invariance test only proves that extra fields do not affect the decision.
